32: Many Punjabis went to Canada and the US for land and jobs; many were ex-soldiers of the British Empire.
The revolutionary strand of the Swadeshi Movement (1905-11) inspired them, above all the Delhi Conspiracy Case 1912, which targeted Viceroy Hardinge 10-16.
Tarak Nath Das wrote Free Hindustan (1907) in Vancouver; G.D. Kumar wrote Swadesh Sevak (1909) in Canada and asked Indian troops to revolt.
Hardayal founded the Bakunin Institute in 1912, a monastery of anarchism.
Baba Gurdit Singh chartered the Japanese ship Komagata Maru from Hong Kong to challenge Canada's direct-journey rule.
WWI began on 28 July 1914, and Britain was stretched on many fronts with fewer British Indian Army units in India.
In August 1914 Bengal revolutionaries, helped by insider Shrish Chandra Mitra and Haridas Datta, diverted one of seven bullock carts of German arms from the Calcutta Customs House.
Plot 1: RB Bose's Punjab mutiny set for 21 Feb 1915. Plot 2: the Pacific arms plot (Apr to Jul 1915), 30,000 rifles via the SS Maverick.
The Punjab mutiny was pre-empted, the arms ships were intercepted, and British intelligence cracked the Christmas plot's codes.
The Defence of India Act 1915 and the First Lahore Conspiracy Case destroyed the organisation in India.
33: Tilak came back from Mandalay in 1914 after six years in prison. Extremists and Revolutionaries had been crushed.
Tilak wanted the Extremists back inside INC, because outside it the British could repress them easily.
Annie Besant, an Irish woman inspired by Home Rule in Ireland and head of the Theosophical Society at Madras, joined INC in 1914. She pushed for Extremist re-entry but Pherozshah Mehta blocked it.
Tilak set up the Indian Home Rule League in April 1916, with 6 branches and headquarters at Poona.
Tilak's rallying cry was 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'. He also demanded vernacular education, linguistic provinces and an end to untouchability.
Tilak ran Kesari (Marathi) and Maharatta (English). Besant ran New India and Commonweal, from which came the word Commonwealth.
WWI brought inflation and anger among the masses. Besant was arrested and interned in 1917. Moderates now joined the Leagues, Sir S.
The Montague Statement of 1917 was a Divide and Rule tactic: Swaraj would come gradually. Extremists proposed Passive Resistance, meaning boycott plus deliberate law-breaking.
By 1917-18 the British had repressed the Leagues and they became defunct. They failed to build a mass movement, and Lower Castes in Madras stayed away.
INC and ML1906 gave joint demands to the British for the first time: separate electorates, an elected majority, 50% Indians in the VEC, broad direct franchise, and early self-government.
Bengal Partition annulled (1911), Italy took Libya (1911), the first Balkan War (1912) and WW1 (1914) pushed the League towards INC.
